title: Prepositions: on, under, in, to
keyIdea: Prepositions are little words that tell where something is or which way it goes. Position words such as on, under, in and next to say where a thing is. Direction words such as to, from, into, out of and off say which way it moves. Many come in opposite pairs: in and out, on and off, up and down, to and from.

kid: Some little words tell where things are. The cat is on the mat. The ball is under the bed. The fish is in the bowl.
Next to means at the side. The cup is next to the plate. They sit side by side.
Some little words tell which way to go. The frog hops off the log. It jumps into the pond. Then it hops to the flower.
Some of these words are opposites. In and out. On and off. Up and down. To and from.
adult: A preposition links a noun to the rest of a sentence, usually to show place, direction or time. US Common Core asks kindergarteners to use the most frequent prepositions (to, from, in, out, on, off, for, of, by, with) and first graders to use frequently occurring prepositions such as during, beyond and toward. In England, children meet position and direction language in Year 1 maths and use prepositions in writing from Year 3.

A preposition plus its noun group is a prepositional phrase: 'under the bed', 'into the pond'. Young children understand these from action first, so moving real objects to follow a spoken phrase is the best practice. Contrast pairs (in versus on, to versus from) build precision faster than single words.

Common mistakes: mixing up in and on (in means inside, on means on top of a surface); using next to and behind as if they meant the same; thinking 'off' only means a switch, not moving down from something; and mixing up to and from, which point opposite ways. Say the phrase and act it out to check.

In the lab your child drags a cat on, under, in and next to; names where a ball is; matches opposite pairs; hops a frog off a log, into a pond, out of it and to a flower; and follows tidy-up instructions.

familyTip: Play 'Teddy says': ask your child to put a teddy on the chair, under the table, in a box and next to the door. Then swap roles so your child gives you the instructions.

visual.caption: Does each word tell where it is, or which way it goes? Drag each word, or tap it and then tap a box.

lab.caption: Flagship lab: move the cat, say where the ball is, match opposites, hop the frog and tidy the room.

practice.prompt: The book sits on top of the table. Which words tell where?
practice.hint: Is the book on top, inside, or below?
practice.explain: On the table. On means on top. In is inside, and under is below.

practice.prompt: There are {n} socks inside the drawer. Where are the socks?
practice.hint: Inside means the same as which little word?
practice.explain: The {n} socks are in the drawer. In means inside.

practice.prompt: What is the opposite of in?
practice.hint: Think of going in a door, then the other way.
practice.explain: Out is the opposite of in. You go in the door, then you come out.

practice.prompt: {n} ducks walk ___ the pond and splash. Which word fits?
practice.hint: Splash means they go in the water.
practice.explain: The {n} ducks walk into the pond. Into means going inside it.

pool.prompt: The dog sleeps below the table. Which words tell where?
pool.hint: Below means the same as which word?
pool.explain: Under the table. Under means below.

pool.prompt: What is the opposite of on?
pool.hint: You put a hat on. Then you take it ...
pool.explain: Off is the opposite of on. You put a hat on, then take it off.

pool.prompt: Mia stands at the side of her friend. Where is she?
pool.hint: At the side means the same as which words?
pool.explain: Next to her friend. Next to means at the side.

pool.prompt: The cat jumps down from the wall. Which words tell which way?
pool.hint: Moving down and away from the top is which word?
pool.explain: Off the wall. Off means moving down and away from the top of something.

pool.prompt: {n} children walk ___ school in the morning. Which word fits?
pool.hint: In the morning they are going towards school.
pool.explain: The {n} children walk to school. To means going towards it.

pool.prompt: Put the ball in the box. Where does it go?
pool.hint: Think about what the little word in means.
pool.explain: Inside the box. In means inside. On top would be on, and beside would be next to.

pool.prompt: {n} fish swim ___ the net and get away. Which word fits?
pool.hint: They get away, so are they going inside or leaving?
pool.explain: The {n} fish swim out of the net. Out of means leaving the inside.
